:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Here, we just take the constant out of the derivative and use the result for the derivative of $\csc x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2csc⁡x) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(csc⁡x) \\  & =2(-csc⁡xcot⁡x) \\  & =-2csc⁡xcot⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Cosecant Function

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: Find $\dfrac {\textrm d y} {\textrm d x}$ if $y = 2x - 3\cot x.$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x-3cot⁡x) \\  & =2-3(-{csc}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =2+3{csc}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Cotangent Function

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
We use the product rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(xsec⁡x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)\cdot sec⁡x+x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(sec⁡x) \\  & =(1)\cdot sec⁡x+x\cdot (sec⁡xtan⁡x) \\  & =sec⁡x(1+xtan⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: Find the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ if $f(x) = \dfrac{-2\cot x}{\sin x}.$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we calculate the derivative using the quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{-2cot⁡x}{sin⁡x}) \\  & =\frac{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2cot⁡x)\cdot sin⁡x-(-2cot⁡x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(sin⁡x)}{{[sin⁡x]}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-2(-{csc}^{2}⁡x)\cdot sin⁡x+2cot⁡x\cdot (cos⁡x)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{2csc⁡x+2cot⁡xcos⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{2csc⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+2cot⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})cos⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})}{{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot (\sqrt{2})+2\cdot (1)\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}{{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{(\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =6\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
